title: Foreign orbiters verify the terrain
verdict: CONFIRMED REAL TERRAIN - backdrop claim falsified. Skylines in two 1971 Apollo 15 surface photographs match the horizon computed from JAXA's 2008 Kaguya/SELENE Terrain Camera DEM to 0.017 deg RMS (flag frame) and 0.21 deg (Rover frame), with best-fit azimuths exactly at the documented viewing directions.
headline: The 2008 Japanese Kaguya DEM reproduces the 1971 Apollo 15 flag-salute skyline to 0.017 deg RMS - 1.3 pixels on the film scan, across 46 deg of panorama, r = 0.99998 - locking AS15-88-11866 onto Mons Hadley Delta at azimuth 184.2 deg, 45.6x better than the best rival azimuth anywhere else on the 360 deg circle; AS15-86-11603 corroborates at 0.208 deg on Mons Hadley at 46.3 deg. Both land exactly where the mission record says the cameras pointed, on mountains the DEM shows are 17-20 km away and 3.5-4.1 km high.
impressive: results/overlay_AS15-88-11866.png - the famous flag-salute photograph with the skyline predicted from the 2008 Japanese orbiter DEM drawn over it: the green curve rides the photographed ridge of Mons Hadley Delta across the whole frame to within 1.3 film pixels (RMS 0.017 deg, r = 0.99998), passing behind the LM and reappearing on the low ridge beyond the Rover.

details.method: photo skyline pixels -> 3D rays (focal 61.1 mm calibrated, pixel scale from the film's 10 mm reseau grid = 75.2 px/mm); fit only camera yaw/pitch/roll by minimizing RMS vs the DEM-rendered 360-deg horizon (curvature drop d^2/2R included, R = 1737.4 km). Each refinement box is re-centred until its optimum is interior, so no reported pose is a clipped boundary value; the best rival azimuth (>10 deg away) is refined identically so rms_contrast compares like with like.
details.uniqueness_note: The two frames carry different weight. AS15-88-11866 is decisive: no other azimuth on the circle comes within 45x of its residual. AS15-86-11603 is corroborating only: its best rival (az 182.5 deg) reaches 0.266 deg RMS with r = 0.9955 - a nominally higher correlation than the winning fit - so a 29-deg stretch of ridge does not pin the azimuth on shape alone; what it shows is that the global optimum still falls at the documented direction.
